US-119-HR10590.description: To establish a pilot program under which the Secretary of Veterans Affairs makes direct housing loans to veterans in rural areas for the construction of new homes.
US-119-HR10590.aiSummary: The bill would start a pilot program where the Department of Veterans Affairs makes direct home loans to veterans in rural areas so they can buy land and build a new home. The loans would have 1% interest, and the home would have to be the veteran’s main residence for at least 24 months; the bill also calls for provided blueprints, help with permits, and the use of domestic wood products in the build. It would set aside $5 million for fiscal year 2027, and the loan authority would end five years after the law takes effect.

US-119-S550.title: A bill to provide for the equitable settlement of certain Indian land disputes regarding land in Illinois, and for other purposes.
US-119-S550.summary:
This bill confers jurisdiction to the U.S. Court of Federal Claims for the Miami Tribe of Oklahoma's land claim arising under the Treaty of Grouseland. The court must render judgement without regard to the statute of limitations or any delay-based defense. This jurisdiction expires unless such a claim is filed within one year.
All other claims, including any future claims, of the tribe to land in Illinois are extinguished.

US-119-S550.aiSummary: The law lets the U.S. Court of Federal Claims hear one land claim by the Miami Tribe of Oklahoma about land in Illinois under the Treaty of Grouseland. The court must decide the claim without using time-limit or delay defenses, and the claim must be filed within one year. It also ends other present and future land claims by the tribe in Illinois.

US-119-HR10095.title: To amend the Foreign Service Act of 1980 to provide per diem eligibility for required leave of members of the Foreign Service.

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10095.aiSummary: The bill would change the Foreign Service Act so Foreign Service members who are ordered to take required leave could get daily pay and related travel help, including lodging and other benefits. It would affect members of the Foreign Service who must take that leave.
